raw_case_text:
A 61-year-old man with past medical history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease for 20 years and hepatic hydatid cyst surgery for 4 years ago presented to the emergency department of Taleghani hospital; a teaching referral hospital in Tehran, Iran, with recurrent abdominal pain aggravated by ingestion, obstructive jaundice, lower limbs edema and abdominal distention. On admission, he denied systemic symptoms like fever, chills and malaise. His vital signs were as follows: blood pressure 120/75 mmhg, heart rate 85 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 per minute and O2 saturation 95% breathing room air. Before admission, his clinical scenario suggestive of biliary involvement made physicians proceed with an outpatient abdominopelvic ultrasound which revealed heterogeneous parenchymal echo pattern of liver with a large amount of ascites indicating the presence of concurrent cirrhosis and a heterogeneous 5.2x4.5cm cystic lesion with sharply defined but irregular borders in liver segment VIII. Common bile duct was reported dilated in proximal part and some sludge was detected in gallbladder. Serum aminotransferases demonstrated an elevation of about 3 times the upper limit of normal. Blood tests revealed a remarkable increase in ALP level up to 5 times the upper limit of normal. A total bilirubin level of 8.9 mg/dl was reported of which direct bilirubin 6.1 mg/dl was. Serum CA19-9 level was normal. Further evaluations by abdominopelvic CT scan were in line with ultrasonographic study. A CT scan revealed moderate ascites, increased gastrointestinal wall thickness, moderate generalized dilation of intra hepatic ducts, common bile duct and common hepatic duct with heterogeneous intraluminal filling defects and a 5.4x4cm-cystic lesion in right liver lobe adjacent to the scar of previous surgery with few calcified foci in its wall. An enlarged gallbladder with a dense layer in the neck suggestive of biliary sludge was also seen. Hydatid cyst treatment by albendazole 400 mg/BD started and he was transferred to the referral hospital for further evaluation and management of choledocholithiasis and cirrhosis. At the first day of admission, he was clearly jaundiced and his vital signs were stable. Ascites analysis revealed a high SAAG and low protein fluid with negative cytology for malignancy suggestive of cirrhosis necessitating a secondary work up.
Given biliary obstruction, the patient underwent an ERCP. Duodenoscopy was then performed Common bile duct was measured 20mm with multiple large filling defects. We then performed dilation with balloon TTS 12-15 and more than 20 pigmented stones, sludge and pus were extracted by balloon. Finally, a 7cm, 10Fr-plastic stent was inserted. Another abdominopelvic CT scan was demanded as presented in figures 1-3.
In spite of biliary stent placement, he continued to remain icterus. We decided to proceed with another ERCP. The procedure revealed more than 30 pigmented stones and hydatid cysts membranes in common bile duct which were extracted completely. An extracted stone has been disclosed in figure-4. Given the patient's clinical picture, laboratory results, imaging and ERCP findings in addition to negative secondary work -ups for cirrhosis, we suspected a diagnosis of hydatid cyst with cystobiliary fistula formation resulting in a portal hypertension and cirrhosis. Portal hypertension is said to be one of the rare complications of hydatid cyst. It has been reported in cases afflicted by cysts involving liver hilum making a compression on porta hepatis or invading inferior vena cava. Portal hypertension in the mentioned case is suggested to come out of a durable cystobiliary communication and its resultant biliary cirrhosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 61-year-old man with a history of hepatic hydatid cyst surgery presented with recurrent postprandial abdominal pain, obstructive jaundice, abdominal distension, and lower-limb edema.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department with recurrent abdominal pain aggravated by food intake, progressive obstructive jaundice, abdominal distension, and bilateral lower-extremity edema.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for 20 years and hepatic hydatid cyst surgery 4 years earlier.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for postprandial abdominal pain, jaundice, abdominal distension, and lower-limb edema; negative for fever, chills, or malaise.

objective.physical_examination: Clearly jaundiced with stable vital signs: blood pressure 120/75 mmHg, heart rate 85 bpm, respiratory rate 16/min, and SpO2 95% on room air. Abdominal distension (ascites) and lower extremity edema were present.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed serum aminotransferases elevated to ~3x ULN, ALP elevated to 5x ULN, total bilirubin 8.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL, and normal serum CA 19-9. Diagnostic paracentesis revealed a high serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG), low ascitic protein, and negative cytology consistent with portal hypertension/cirrhosis. Outpatient abdominopelvic ultrasound showed a cirrhotic liver, large-volume ascites, proximal CBD dilatation, gallbladder sludge, and a 5.2 x 4.5 cm heterogeneous cystic lesion in hepatic segment VIII.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominopelvic CT confirmed moderate ascites, generalized intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary dilatation with intraluminal filling defects, gallbladder sludge, and a 5.4 x 4 cm focally calcified cystic lesion in segment VIII adjacent to the prior surgical scar. Initial ERCP showed a 20-mm dilated CBD with multiple filling defects; balloon sweep extracted >20 pigmented stones, sludge, and pus, and a 7-cm 10Fr plastic stent was placed. Due to persistent jaundice, a second ERCP extracted >30 additional pigmented stones and intrabiliary hydatid cyst membranes from the common bile duct.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Recurrent/residual segment VIII hepatic hydatid cyst with chronic cystobiliary fistula complicated by intrabiliary rupture, choledocholithiasis (>50 pigmented stones and hydatid membranes), secondary biliary cirrhosis, and portal hypertension, confirmed on repeat ERCP extraction of hydatid membranes from the CBD. Managed with oral albendazole (400 mg twice daily) and two sequential therapeutic ERCPs achieving complete biliary clearance.
